name: Ryokan Ashgrey Slub Henley
description:
Ryokan is a small-batch label operating out of a workshop in the Midmarket district, making garments that sit at the intersection of Japanese workwear restraint and the kind of soft, worn-in quality associated with American heritage clothing — a combination that feels natural in a city where cultural boundaries dissolved long ago. The Ashgrey Slub Henley is their signature piece: a three-button henley in a slubby cotton-analog that has an irregular, slightly textured surface suggesting handmade without claiming it. The fit is relaxed through the chest and shoulders, slightly tapered at the waist. The grey is not a clean grey — it has depth, warmth, the quality of something that was once another color and has arrived here through time.

It's the kind of shirt that people who care about clothes recognize immediately and people who don't care about clothes never notice. The stitching is tight, the seams are clean, the collar won't deform. Ryokan makes two hundred of these per season. They sell out in days. No advertising.
what_it_says: You know what you're looking at. You don't need to explain it to anyone who doesn't.
worn_by: people with strong opinions about fabric
anyone who found Ryokan through a friend who found them through another friend
story_hooks: Ryokan's founder has been offered corponation buyouts four times. Each time he's declined. After the last offer, his workshop's lease was quietly not renewed. He's been operating month-to-month from a secondary location he won't disclose.

A specific run of Ashgrey Henleys from the 2198 season has a dye lot error that makes them a very slightly different shade — almost imperceptible, but wearers can tell. This run has become sought-after.
Someone is wearing a Ryokan Ashgrey Henley in a photograph taken at a crime scene. The shirt is real. The person wearing it has no documented identity.
